title: Recover the Permutation From the XORs of Neighbours

concept.title: The XOR of all numbers is known; the XORs of the pairs at odd positions give everything except the first number
body: A hidden permutation `p` of the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` (where `n` is **odd**) is lost. What remains is the list `e` of the XORs of neighbours: `e[i] = p[i] ^ p[i+1]`, with `n - 1` numbers. The permutation is uniquely determined by `e`. For `e = 3 1` the answer is `1 2 3`: `1 ^ 2 = 3` and `2 ^ 3 = 1`. Knowing the first number `p[0]`, everything follows: `p[i+1] = p[i] ^ e[i]`.

To find the first number use two XORs. First, the XOR of **all** the numbers of a permutation of `1..n` is known without the permutation: `T = 1 ^ 2 ^ ... ^ n`. Second, take `e[1] ^ e[3] ^ e[5] ^ ...` (the elements at odd positions). Since `e[1] = p[1] ^ p[2]`, `e[3] = p[3] ^ p[4]`, ..., and `n - 1` is even, these pairs cover **all the numbers except `p[0]`**: `p[1] ^ p[2] ^ ... ^ p[n-1]`. This is where the oddness of `n` is used.

body.code:
n = m + 1
total = 0
for v in range(1, n + 1): total ^= v          # XOR of 1..n
odd = 0
for i in range(1, m, 2): odd ^= e[i]          # XOR of p[1] .. p[n-1]
first = total ^ odd                            # everything cancels except p[0]
p = [first]
for x in e: p.append(p[-1] ^ x)
print(*p)

body: Both XORs take O(n) and rebuilding the permutation takes O(n), so the whole solution is linear. It uses three properties of XOR together: it is its own inverse, it is associative and commutative (so the pairs can be regrouped), and a full permutation has a known total.

statement: A permutation `p` of the numbers 1, 2, ..., n (n odd) is hidden. You are given the n - 1 numbers `e[i] = p[i] ^ p[i+1]`. Print the permutation `p` (it is unique).
inputFormat: The first line has `m`: the length of the list of XORs (it is even).
The second line has `m` numbers: `e[i] = p[i] ^ p[i+1]`.
outputFormat: Print the `n` numbers of the permutation on one line, separated by spaces.
constraints: The hidden permutation `p` has `n = m + 1` numbers (odd) and contains each of 1..n exactly once.
hints: Once p[0] is known, p[i+1] = p[i] ^ e[i].
XOR all numbers 1..n to get the total of the permutation.
XOR the elements of e at odd positions to get the XOR of all numbers except p[0].

explanation: The first number is the XOR of 1..n XOR-ed with the XOR of the elements of e at odd positions (which equals the XOR of all numbers except the first); the rest follows from p[i+1] = p[i] ^ e[i].

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

m = int(input())
e = list(map(int, input().split()))

n = m + 1
total = 0
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    total ^= v
odd = 0
for i in range(1, m, 2):
    odd ^= e[i]
p = [total ^ odd]
for x in e:
    p.append(p[-1] ^ x)
print(*p)
